claims.text: The starting nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 alloy has a single-phase BCC matrix.
Cr–V-rich precipitates begin to form in nanocrystalline W38Ta36Cr15V11 at approximately 8 dpa.
Approximately 2 at% Re will be incorporated into W38Ta36Cr15V11 during synthesis.
Magnetron sputtering or powder metallurgy can produce a homogeneous distribution of Re in the proposed alloy's BCC matrix.
Controlled processing can retain approximately 2 at% Re as a supersaturated solute in the BCC matrix.
Uniformly dispersed Re atoms act as vacancy traps in the irradiated alloy.
Re is a high-melting refractory element.
Re preferentially interacts with vacancies.
Vacancy trapping by Re reduces the irradiation-enhanced diffusion rates of Cr and V.
Reduced Cr and V diffusion suppresses Cr–V clustering and precipitation during irradiation.
The Re-modified alloy will have a significantly lower Cr–V precipitate density, or no detectable Cr–V precipitates, at 8 dpa relative to the unmodified alloy.
The Re-modified alloy will retain minimal irradiation-induced hardening relative to the unmodified alloy.
The Re-modified alloy will preserve high radiation resistance.
The Re-modified alloy will remain compatible with scalable bulk processing.
Cr–V precipitation in unmodified W38Ta36Cr15V11 causes increased hardening and brittleness.
Dispersed precipitates can obstruct dislocation motion, increasing strength while also promoting brittleness.
The claimed suppression effect is limited to doses up to approximately 8 dpa and specimen temperatures at or below 600 °C.
Re may form undesired secondary phases if processing is not optimized.
TEM and APT measurements can test whether Re addition reduces precipitate size or number density relative to an identically processed control.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant reduction in Cr–V precipitation, or observation of greater irradiation hardening than in the control, falsifies the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The hypothesis describes the intervention as preserving the baseline alloy's low irradiation hardening, whereas the baseline field says Cr–V precipitation in the unmodified alloy leads to increased hardening and brittleness.
